transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been having trouble stopping myself from taking on things. Like, I’ll start making big work plans, then certification schedules, then decide I need to redo the home network, and I’m messaging old contacts about ideas. It just builds and builds, and I don’t really stop at normal limits. Usually my wife or my director has to step in and tell me to slow down.
During these times, have you ever heard or seen things that other people didn’t, or become convinced of something others said wasn’t true?

Yes. During the times when I’m really wound up and barely sleeping, I’ve heard things in the background noise, like the server fans or equipment hum, almost like comments were being made. And I’ve also read work messages like they had hidden threats in them, even when other people said that wasn’t what was there.
Have you had other times like this when you felt unusually energized and driven, but did not hear things or feel messages had hidden threats?

Yes. There are times where I’m really energized and driven, but it’s not like I’m hearing things or reading hidden meanings. I’ll just feel like I can’t stop moving—pacing around the house with my laptop, reorganizing the garage, rewriting project boards. If I try to just sit and watch a show, I feel physically uncomfortable, like I need to be doing something.
Have you ever had a period when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yes. I do have stretches like that where most days I wake up feeling like I’m just… a failed version of myself. Everything feels heavy and flat, and even answering normal questions from my wife can feel like too much.
During one of those high-energy times, were you ever hospitalized because of it?
I don’t think I have anything specific to say about that. I’m not sure—nothing comes to mind clearly.
During one of your high-energy periods, did it ever get so severe that you couldn't function normally at work or at home?

Yes. It’s gotten bad enough that I wasn’t really functioning normally. At work, after a migration failed, I was put on leave. And at home my wife has had to step in with things like my spending, me working late into the night, and conversations turning into arguments. I’ve also pulled back from church music, climbing, and mentoring because I just can’t reliably show up or follow through.
During those high-energy periods, do you feel unusually euphoric or unusually irritable?

Yes. Some weeks I feel almost electric, like I can do anything and nothing can stop me. But it can flip into irritability really fast—like if there’s a small delay, or my wife asks me a simple question, I snap because it feels like people are trying to slow me down on purpose.
Have you ever heard those comments or felt messages had hidden threats when you were not in one of those high-energy, barely-sleeping periods?

Yes. That’s happened even when I wasn’t in one of those high-energy phases. There have been stretches where I felt pretty calm or kind of flat—not especially up or depressed—and I still thought Teams statuses were coded warnings. I also heard brief comments when nobody was there. Sometimes that lasted a few weeks at a time.
Have you ever had those voices or coded-warning beliefs continue for 2 weeks or longer during a time when you were not feeling especially up, irritable, or depressed?

Yes. There have been a few times like that, where I was more calm or just kind of flat—not really up, not depressed—and it still kept going. I’d still think Teams statuses had coded warnings in them, and I’d hear short comments when nobody was actually there. Some of those stretches lasted a few weeks.
